content.text: You already run Postgres and nothing else. Three options: (1) add Redis and BullMQ, the most common setup; (2) use a Postgres-backed queue like pg-boss, no new infrastructure; (3) a hosted scheduler like a cron service hitting an endpoint. I'd lean Redis + BullMQ since it's the standard and has a nice dashboard.

message.content: No Redis. We're 7 people and nobody wants to run another piece of infra. What does pg-boss cost us?

content.text: pg-boss stores jobs in a table in your existing database. Costs: some write load on Postgres, and throughput tops out in the low thousands of jobs per minute, which is far above a weekly digest. Retries and scheduling are built in.

message.content: Fine. pg-boss it is. If we ever need more than a few thousand jobs a minute or jobs start slowing the main DB we revisit. Hosted cron is out too, I don't want the digest depending on a third party being up.

content.text: Going with pg-boss on the existing Postgres. I'll add a worker process and schedule the digest job for Monday 9am.
